Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few answers from our side: 

Quick answers
- Buying preference: Our procurement team strongly prefers AWS Marketplace where possible because it simplifies internal chargeback and tagging; they are open to a private offer.
- Procurement process: Primary procurement contact: Matt Reynolds (cc'd). We issue POs on a Net30 cadence; smaller pilots sometimes go on card but for anything expected to exceed $2.5k/month we need a PO.
- Invoice requirements: We need department and cost-center fields on invoices; I'll get the exact template if helpful.

Security/compliance
- SOC 2 summary is required; our legal will want more detail about data residency and logs retention for audit readiness.

Next logistical asks
1) Can you outline differences between (A) AWS Marketplace private offer, (B) direct PO to Redwood invoiced, and (C) card payments for the pilot — specifically around billing cadence, refund/credits, and how unit pricing is represented on invoices?
2) If Marketplace private offer is the right path, what info do you need from our procurement team to set that up?

I can pull the procurement PO template and share it by end of day. If convenient, Matt and I can join a 30-minute call with your finance/legal to line up expectations.

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Sophie — great to hear marketplace is preferred. Below is a concise comparison and what we typically need to make each path smooth.

High-level comparison
A) AWS Marketplace private offer
- How billing appears: Charges flow through AWS billing; you receive a single AWS invoice with Redwood line items (private offer maps SKU to pricing).
- Pros: Matches internal chargeback; consistent AWS terms; simplifies accounting.
- Cons: Takes additional steps to set up a private offer and associate accounts; possible lag on first invoice cycle.
- What we need from you: AWS org/account ID, procurement contact, PO template for private offer, expected start date.

B) Direct PO to Redwood (invoice)
- How billing appears: Redwood sends monthly invoices directly to Orbit Health; we can pre-fill cost-center fields you need.
- Pros: Quicker to stand up for pilots; flexible invoice line items.
- Cons: Procurement may prefer marketplace for internal policies.

C) Card payments
- Best for short, low-dollar pilots (<$2.5k/month).

What I’ll do next
- I’ll upload an initial Mutual Action Plan (attached) with suggested owners and dates; Karthik will validate technical gating items once we confirm the procurement route.
- Please share the procurement PO template and your AWS account ID if you want us to pursue a private offer.

Proposed timeline
- By EOD tomorrow: Orbit shares PO template + AWS account ID (if private offer), or confirm direct PO intent.
- This week: 30-minute meeting with your procurement + our finance/ops to finalize paperwork.

Hi Sophie — quick technical checklist while procurement gets sorted: 

Technical items we usually validate for AWS Marketplace/private offer path
- SSO / IdP: confirm SAML provider and whether you require SCIM provisioning or just SSO for admin console.
- KMS / key management: do you require customer-managed keys for any storage or can Redwood-managed encryption suffice for the trial?
- Region: are workloads constrained to us-east-1 / us-west-2 for latency/compliance?
- Audit logs: retention window required by your audit team (we typically keep 90 days by default; can extend).

If you can share the PO template and AWS org/account ID, I’ll block 30 minutes for a technical readiness call (I can do Wed/Thu afternoon PT).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
